text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-About 74 percent of the Lebanese are against the decision of the government to ban a large number of television and radio stations. Some 75 percent say the audiovisual media must be organised.
-A national meeting grouping representatives of political parties, media proprietors and employees said they might resort to strikes and demonstrations to protest against the government's decision.
-Assistant U.S. Secretary of State Pelletreau: "Lebanon First" was not proposed seriously.

-Acting Finance Minister Siniora and U.S. ambassador Jones prepare for the meetings of the consultative committee formed under the terms of the April ceasefire understanding between Israel and Lebanon.
-The ceasefire monitoring committee to meet again next Tuesday.
-Kuwait, Lebanon and Egypt stock exchanges signed an agreement to prepare for crosslisting. Total capitalisation of the three markets is $31 billion.
-Lebanon's Christian external opposition and their local ally Chamoun: Forged elections aim at destroying Lebanon's sovereignty and independence.
